title: Version claims
oneLiner: Every launcher start in a relocated root marks its version as in use, so a later prune can tell which versions' entries are still wanted.

abstractions.name: VersionClaim
abstractions.responsibility: A claim's identity, `<version>.<launcher-id>`, and the one rule that parses and validates its name.

abstractions.name: FreshVersions
abstractions.responsibility: The versions a prune must keep: every valid claim inside the window, plus the running version.

abstractions.name: RootRetention::claim_running_version
abstractions.responsibility: Writes the running version's claim at start-up in a relocated root; does nothing in the plugin's own `bin/`.

decisions.decision: Record use as a claim file's mtime, refreshed at most every 1.4 days
alternatives: a registry file listing installed versions, rewritten under a lock
rewrite the claim on every invocation
decisions.rationale: An empty file per install needs no lock and no parsing, a read-only root still dispatches, and the throttle keeps a warm start to one `lstat` almost every time.
decisions.consequences: Protection ends 12.6 to 14 days after last use, not exactly 14, and launchers from before claims write none, so their entries are evicted (an accepted risk).
decisions.note: The right trade for the warm path. The fail-open `lstat` at `version_claims.rs:138` is a defect in the reader, not in this decision.

decisions.decision: Claim per install, not per version
alternatives: one claim per version, shared by every install of it
decisions.rationale: Two installs of one version refresh independently, so one going idle cannot expire the other's protection, and a stale twin can go without touching the live one.
decisions.consequences: The `<version>.<launcher-id>` name becomes a contract between releases; changing it strands every existing claim.

purpose: A relocated root outlives every plugin version that shares it, and several versions use it at once: a session started before an upgrade keeps its version until it reloads. "Keep the newest N versions" would evict a version a live session still dispatches. A claim gives each install a heartbeat, so a prune keeps what is still in use and treats everything else as unclaimed.
mechanism: A claim is an empty file, `claims/<version>.<launcher-id>`; only its mtime carries meaning. Start-up refreshes it, in a relocated root only, at most every 1.4 days, and swallows any failure (the sequence above). A prune reads `claims/` into a `ClaimsListing` that is either `Read(claims)` or `Unreadable(kind)`, so "no claims" is never confused with "could not look". `FreshVersions` keeps every version with a valid claim inside the window, plus the running version. An unknown or future mtime counts as fresh, so clock skew can only keep entries, never remove them.

beforeAfter.aspect: What keeps an old version's single-file entries in a relocated root
beforeAfter.before: Nothing ever removed them, so they stayed for ever.
beforeAfter.after: A valid claim refreshed inside the window, or being the running version; otherwise they go once 1 h old.

beforeAfter.aspect: Start-up filesystem work in a relocated root
beforeAfter.after: One `lstat` of the claim; `mkdir`, a trust check, a write and `set_modified` at most once per 1.4 days.

domain.meaning: Empty file `claims/<version>.<launcher-id>` whose mtime records when that install last refreshed it.
16 lowercase hex: the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the launcher's `current_exe()` path.
How long a claim protects: `CLAIM_WINDOW` (14 days), or `--older-than` seconds for the verb.

invariants.text: In a relocated root the running version's claim is refreshed before any lookup can store an entry.
A valid claim younger than the refresh interval is not rewritten.
A failed claim refresh never fails a dispatch.

risks.text: A claim whose `lstat` fails for any reason is silently dropped while the listing stays `Read`, so that version reads as unclaimed and its aged entries go. It needs `claims/` to lose its search bit while staying readable, or I/O errors; the cost is a re-fetch, not data loss.

Launchers built before this change write no claims, so every claim-aware prune evicts their entries once they are 1 h old, and they cannot re-resolve a vanished entry. Only 1.24.0 pre-releases ship a launcher (v1.23.0 has no `cli/` or `bin/accelerator`), so the exposure is pre-release users with `ACCELERATOR_CACHE_DIR` set.

stops.title: The windows every prune shares
stops.fit: The clock the whole retention design runs on: claims are written against `CLAIM_WINDOW`, `FreshVersions` keeps what falls inside it, and both single-file and tree prune age their entries by `AGE_BACKSTOP`. Every later stop either writes a claim or reads one against these windows.
stops.note: `AGE_BACKSTOP` (1 h), `CLAIM_WINDOW` (14 days) and `REFRESH_FRACTION` (10) sit in a leaf module so single-file and tree prune share them without importing each other. `is_aged` is `>=` the backstop, false for an unknown mtime and age zero for a future one, so clock trouble can only keep. Claims use the opposite edge: a claim exactly at the window is stale, because `FreshVersions::within` tests `<`.
stops.check: `is_aged` is the age test for entries and residue at `single_file.rs:391`, `residue.rs:78` and `residue.rs:122`; confirm no other duration is hard-coded in `retention/`.

stops.title: Launcher id: one claim per install
stops.fit: Carries the decision to claim per install rather than per version: the id becomes the `<launcher-id>` half of every `VersionClaim` name, so a prune sees one claim per install of a version and can tell a live install from a removed one.
stops.note: The id hashes the launcher's own path, which is content-addressed, so two installs of one version write distinct claims and one's refresh never masks the other's absence. If `current_exe()` fails, the seed falls back to the version string and such installs share a claim. Only the claim name's shape crosses versions; each launcher only ever writes its own id.

figure.title: One claim per install, not per version

stops.title: Claim path and the version it names
stops.fit: Where a claim's name meets the rest of the root: `claim_running_version` writes this path at start-up, and `FreshVersions` reads the `<version>` half back to decide which launcher entries a prune keeps. It is the seam between writing claims and honouring them.
stops.note: `<version>` is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, but `bin/accelerator` names launcher entries from `plugin.json`'s version (`bin/accelerator:141`). Launcher-entry protection therefore assumes the two strings match. `tasks/version.py:75-88` writes both together, and the entrypoint A/B/C test fails if the running launcher entry is pruned.
stops.check: Is lockstep between `plugin.json` and the `cli/` workspace version enforced anywhere besides `tasks/version.py`?

findingChecks.note: `filesystem.entry(&path).ok()?` at `version_claims.rs:138` drops any claim whose `lstat` fails, and `list` still returns `Read`. With `claims/` at 0600 (owner-only, so trusted; readable but not searchable) every `lstat` fails with `EACCES`, every other version reads as unclaimed and its aged entries go, with no warning. The cost is re-fetching; the running version stays protected.

`version_claims::list` and `tree::claims::list` share their shape but diverge: an untrusted version-claims directory becomes `Unreadable(PermissionDenied)` and prints as "claims unreadable (permission denied)", where tree claims report `Untrusted`; a `readdir` `NotFound` is empty here but `Unreadable` there. Both carry the same per-claim `lstat` gap, so one shared reader would fix R1-06 and R1-08 together.

ownNotes.text: A version stops being fresh 12.6 to 14 days after its last use, not 14: the throttle lets a claim be up to 1.4 days old at the version's last start. `internals.md:329` ("a version idle for 14 days, whose claim is that old") states a sufficient condition, not the actual one.

signOff: Do you accept that a version's protection is a heartbeat fresh for 12.6 to 14 days after its last use, and that until R1-06 is fixed a per-claim `lstat` failure fails open?
